children: The FTSE MIB fell to around 52,300 on Monday, giving back some of last week’s gains, with technology-related stocks leading losses.
STMicroelectronics and Prysmian fell 4.1% and 5.1%, respectively, as investors reacted to Anthropic’s call over the weekend for a slower pace of AI development amid growing safety concerns.
Risk appetite was also weakened by a renewed surge in oil prices amid escalating Middle East tensions and supply concerns.
Other notable laggards included Enel (-1.0%) and Buzzi Unicem (-1.2%), while most financial stocks also traded lower.

Monte dei Paschi di Siena fell 0.4% and Banco BPM 0.2% after MPS said its offers for Banco BPM and Banca Generali would remain valid even if Intesa Sanpaolo takes control of MPS. MPS said the implied premiums stood at 3.4% for Banco BPM and 12.8% for Banca Generali as of September 11.

title: FTSE MIB Declines on Monday
